s1.syndrome_frame: Acute lower abdominal pain with nausea and vomiting in a young female
salient_findings: Cystic mass arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex
key_facts: 3-day history of nausea, vomiting, and right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Negative urine human chorionic gonadotropin test
Second abdominopelvic ultrasound suggestive of retrocecal appendicitis
Cystic mass found arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex during surgery

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute lower abdominal pain with nausea and vomiting in a young female
salient_findings: Cystic mass arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex
key_facts: 3-day history of nausea, vomiting, and right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Negative urine human chorionic gonadotropin test
Second abdominopelvic ultrasound suggestive of retrocecal appendicitis

shortlist.label: Tubo-ovarian abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass with purulent fluid found during surgery

shortlist.label: Ruptured ovarian cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass found arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex

shortlist.label: Ovarian torsion
shortlist.why_kept: Acute lower abdominal pain and nausea in a young female

shortlist.label: Pelvic inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated leukocyte count and C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Ovarian neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass found during surgery, although less likely given the patient's age

raw.rationale: The presence of a cystic mass with purulent fluid arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex, along with elevated leukocyte count and C-reactive protein, supports the diagnosis of a tubo-ovarian abscess.

rejected.label: Ruptured ovarian cyst
rejected.why: The presence of purulent fluid and elevated inflammatory markers suggests an infectious process rather than a simple cyst rupture.

rejected.label: Ovarian torsion
rejected.why: There is no mention of the typical severe, sudden onset pain or the characteristic ultrasound findings of ovarian torsion.

rejected.label: Pelvic inflammatory disease
rejected.why: While PID can cause similar symptoms, the focal nature of the cystic mass and the absence of other signs of pelvic infection make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Ovarian neoplasm
rejected.why: The acute presentation and the presence of purulent fluid are not typical of an ovarian neoplasm, which would more likely present with a solid mass and possibly more chronic symptoms.
